analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read in VM is caused by malformed/truncated bytecode emitted by codegen. In scope_finish(), irep->iseq is shrunk with codegen_realloc using sizeof(mrb_code)*s->pc + catchsize, but no extra terminating instruction is reserved/ensured for the VM fetch path. For the PoC, the generated instruction stream length ends up exactly at allocation boundary (11 bytes), and mrb_vm_exec reads one byte past end while decoding next opcode/immediates (crash observed at vm.c:1183 in OP_LOADI32 decode). Root cause is incorrect final iseq sizing/termination in compiler output, not VM input validation.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Harness mruby_fuzzer calls mrb_load_string() directly on attacker-controlled source. A crafted Ruby snippet (e.g., `3or l=3\nl+=12\n1`) drives parser+codegen through scope_finish(), producing an irep with boundary-length iseq lacking safe termination/padding for subsequent VM decode. When mrb_top_run/mrb_vm_exec executes that irep, instruction fetch/operand decode steps past allocated iseq by 1 byte, triggering ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
